arxiv-2103-10833.title: Effects of coherence on temporal resolution
arxiv-2103-10833.creator: Syamsundar De, Jano Gil-Lopez, Benjamin Brecht, Christine Silberhorn, Luis L. Sánchez-Soto, Zdeněk Hradil, Jaroslav Řeháček
arxiv-2103-10833.description: Abstract Measuring small separations between two optical sources, either in space or in time, constitute an important metrological challenge as standard intensity-only measurements fail for vanishing separations. Contrarily, it has been established that appropriate coherent mode projections can appraise arbitrarily small separations with quantum-limited precision.

arxiv-2105-08647.creator: J. Lorenzo, I. Parra, M. A. Sotelo
arxiv-2105-08647.description: Abstract Understanding pedestrian crossing behavior is an essential goal in intelligent vehicle development, leading to an improvement in their security and traffic flow. In this paper, we developed a method called IntFormer. It is based on transformer architecture and a novel convolutional video classification model called RubiksNet.

arxiv-2309-09822.title: Is the Computing Continuum Already Here?

arxiv-2309-09822.description: Abstract The computing continuum, a novel paradigm that extends beyond the current silos of cloud and edge computing, can enable the seamless and dynamic deployment of applications across diverse infrastructures. By utilizing the cloud-native features and scalability of Kubernetes, this concept promotes deployment transparency, communication transparency, and resource availability transparency.

arxiv-2403-11804.description: Abstract ‘Debris disks’ are collections of small bodies around stars, such as the Asteroid Belt and Kuiper Belt in our Solar System. These disks are composed of objects smaller than planets, including asteroids, comets, dust, and dwarf planets. We detect debris disks around a significant fraction of stars, and these disks appear to be common components of planetary systems.

arxiv-2403-15181.title: A Two Level Neural Approach Combining Off-Chip Prediction with Adaptive Prefetch Filtering
arxiv-2403-15181.creator: Alexandre Valentin Jamet alexandre.jamet@bsc.es, Georgios Vavouliotis georgios.vavouliotis2@huawei.com, Daniel A. Jiménez djimenez@acm.org, Lluc Alvarez lluc.alvarez@bsc.es, Marc Casas marc.casas@bsc.es
arxiv-2403-15181.description: Abstract To alleviate the performance and energy overheads of contemporary applications with large data footprints, we propose the Two Level Perceptron (TLP) predictor, a neural mechanism that effectively combines predicting whether an access will be off-chip with adaptive prefetch filtering at the first-level data cache (L1D).

arxiv-2411-07925.title: Revisiting X-ray Afterglows of Jetted Tidal Disruption Events with the External Reverse Shock
arxiv-2411-07925.creator: Chengchao Yuan (袁成超), Walter Winter, B. Theodore Zhang (张兵), Kohta Murase, Bing Zhang (张冰)
arxiv-2411-07925.description: Abstract We investigate the external reverse shock region of relativistic jets as the origin of X-ray afterglows of jetted tidal disruption events (TDEs) that exhibit luminous jets accompanied by fast-declining non-thermal X-ray emissions. We model the dynamics of jet propagating within an external density medium, accounting for continuous energy injection driven by accretion activities.

arxiv-2502-12328.title: LM Agents for Coordinating Multi-User Information Gathering
arxiv-2502-12328.creator: Harsh Jhamtani, Jacob Andreas, Benjamin Van Durme
arxiv-2502-12328.description: Abstract This paper introduces PeopleJoin , a benchmark for evaluating LM-mediated collaborative problem solving. Given a user request, PeopleJoin agents must identify teammates who might be able to assist, converse with these teammates to gather information, and finally compile a useful answer or summary for the original user.

pmc-11462268.title: Study on Attenuation Characteristics of Reissner’s Membrane Mode in Cochlea
pmc-11462268.creator: Toshiaki Kitamura
pmc-11462268.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Multiple propagation modes progress along the basilar membrane and Reissner’s membrane, called basilar membrane mode (BM mode) and Reissner’s membrane mode (RM mode), respectively.
